title: Four way-too-early questions ahead of the 2027 IndyCar season
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Sunday's season finale at Laguna Seca wrapped up the 2026 NTT IndyCar Series season, with Scott McLaughlin snapping a 35-race winless drought and Alex Palou officially being crowned champion for a fourth consecutive season.

With six months remaining until the 2027 IndyCar campaign begins on March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Fla., here are some early questions swirling around the 2027 season.

Can anyone stop Alex Palou...

Like Thanos, Palou has been inevitable over the past four seasons. The five-time series champion and 2025 Indianapolis 500 winner won six times this season and had 15 top 10s in 18 races, winning the championship by 86 points over Kyle Kirkwood.

Many pundits have pointed to IndyCar's new race car in 2028 as an opportunity for the field to finally beat Palou, but that doesn't mean they won't be trying to best the Spaniard next year. Everyone in the IndyCar paddock had better get to work immediately if they don't want to see Palou win a fifth straight Astor Cup next season?

...and will it be Kyle Kirkwood?

Kirkwood is the obvious choice as the potential villain who could upend Palou's dynasty. The Jupiter, Fla., native won twice this season and matched Palou with 15 top 10s, though the championship was already decided ahead of Sunday's race at Laguna Seca.

If the No. 27 team can find a way to have a four or five-win season in 2027, beating Palou for the championship could become very realistic. Kirkwood has become one of IndyCar's newest superstars and appears to have the best shot at stopping Palou's streak of titles.

How will Scott Dixon, Christian Lundgaard fare with their new teams?

After 25 years with Chip Ganassi Racing, Dixon, who had his first winless season since 2004 this year, will move onto what may or may not be greener pastures at Arrow McLaren next season. The 46-year-old wasn't all that competitive this season, though with a new organization, he could be a dark horse in the title race next year as he looks for a seventh championship.

On the other hand, Arrow McLaren's Christian Lundgaard, who racked up two wins, 14 top 10s and a third-place points finish this season, is yet to announce his destination for 2027, though he's the favorite to land Dixon's old ride at CGR, essentially completing a driver swap between the two organizations. McLaren decided that Lundgaard's performance on ovals leaves something to be desired, but he made strides in that department towards the end of the season and will be in the championship hunt next year.

Can David Malukas finally win a race?

David Malukas' quest to win an IndyCar race hasn't quite been the odyssey that was Dale Earnhardt's attempt to win the Daytona 500, but make no mistake about it, the Chicago native has been through hell and back in his struggle to reach victory lane. From losing the closest Indianapolis 500 in history to Felix Rosenqvist in May to an engine issue that cost him a win at Milwaukee last week, that elusive checkered flag is yet to come for Malukas.

The good news is that the 24-year-old still showed out in his debut season with Team Penske, finishing fifth in the standings with nine top fives and 13 top 10s. He was even second in the standings for a portion of the season. All that's left for him to do is finally win a race, which is proving to be much easier said than done.

title: Scott McLaughlin ends drought in Monterey; Alex Palou revels in 5th title
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Scott McLaughlin ended his 2026 IndyCar season with a long-sought victory at the Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey before Alex Palou lifted the trophy for the series championship Sunday in Monterey, Calif.

Last week, Palou clinched his fourth straight IndyCar championship and fifth in six years with one race to go. The Spaniard won six races and finished the season with 631 points, 86 more than runner-up Kyle Kirkwood.

In the trophy presentation, Palou thanked Chip Ganassi Racing and the team behind his No. 10 DHL Honda.

"I had the rocket ship," Palou said of his racecar. "... Everybody that has been supporting this team and has been part of it. Honda giving us all that power that we needed every single time. Just been a magical year. Thank you all, guys, for being here. It makes it super special, and time to celebrate with all these guys."

At 29, Palou is the youngest driver in IndyCar history to win five season titles. New Zealand's Scott Dixon holds the record with six, while A.J. Foyt won seven championships in the open-wheel racing series that preceded IndyCar.

As for the race at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca -- in which Palou settled for eighth -- McLaughlin was the polesitter and led 87 of the 95 laps for a dominant victory.

The New Zealander had not won a race since Sept. 1, 2024, at the Milwaukee Mile. The 33-year-old dedicated it to his daughter Lucy, who was born in October 2024.

"My little girl hasn't seen me win yet, and now she has," McLaughlin said. "So, Dad's coming home with a trophy, baby. Let's go!

"These guys and girls at Team Penske have stood behind me the whole time. Congrats to Alex on his fifth (championship), but we're working hard to beat them, and today was a big step in the right direction."

Kirkwood came in second, 1.3739 seconds behind, securing enough points to push into second in the final points standings.

"We had an awesome race. We just played it super clean, super methodical," Kirkwood said. "We started on the alts (tires) and actually moved up to third early on and Palou went off-strategy there and we assumed second and just held second the whole time.

"Second place is best of the rest, and has been the real championship the past couple years," he added, referring to Palou's reign of dominance. "So we're happy with it."

Alexander Rossi, Felix Rosenqvist of Sweden and David Malukas rounded out the top five at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.

title: Conor Daly lands full-time IndyCar ride with D&R
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Conor Daly has been named the full-time driver for Dreyer & Reinbold Racing's new IndyCar Series entry in 2027.

Daly, 34, will drive the No. 24 Honda for the Indianapolis-based team that he first raced for at the 2024 Indianapolis 500, where he finished 10th. After racing for Juncos Hollinger Racing in 2025, the Indiana native lost his seat with the team opting to go with Sting Ray Robb and Rinus VeeKay this season.

Daly again competed for D&R at the 2026 Indianapolis 500, qualifying in eighth place and going on to finish 12th. He will now return to the grid full-time next season.

"I'm super pumped," Daly said. "If you knew how hard they've worked behind the scenes. 'Finish the job' is what (Dennis Reinbold) told them to do. To be here, with Honda as well. I want to thank Chevy for all the years I've been with them. This is a huge deal for me to have a multi-year deal, which is the first time in my life."

DRR will work with Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing in a technical alliance.

"Conor has raced for us at Indianapolis, so we know how he prepares, how he works with engineers, and how much he gets out of a car," DRR CEO Derek Reinbold said. "He has shown for years that he can win the Indianapolis 500, and our job is to give him a car that lets him do it. We are building a team that contends every weekend, and Conor is the driver we trust to carry that effort across the full season. An Indiana driver in an Indiana team's car is exactly how we want to come back."

title: Federal Investigation Forces Chevy to Pull the Plug on IndyCar Partnership With Andretti
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Andretti’s relationship with Chevrolet once produced one of the most successful partnerships in IndyCar. When GM returned to the series in 2012, Andretti joined forces with the manufacturer, and Ryan Hunter-Reay delivered a dream start by sweeping the driver’s championship. The partnership, however, did not last, with Andretti eventually returning to Honda power and maintaining that relationship ever since.

That history made recent rumors of a potential Chevrolet-Andretti reunion particularly intriguing. But just as speculation about the two sides working together again began to surface, an alleged decision by GM to step away from new business with the team has thrown fresh uncertainty over the possibility.

“I was told in Milwaukee the recent headlines with TWG owner Mark Walter and the federal investigation into his finances are behind the alleged decision by GM to step away from conducting new business with the [Andretti IndyCar] team,” NASCAR reporter Adam Stern wrote on his X account.

The report comes as Walter’s sprawling business empire faces scrutiny from federal prosecutors and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Walter is the founder and CEO of TWG Global, which has major interests across professional sports and financial services, including the Andretti IndyCar team. The investigation centers largely on the financial dealings of two insurance companies controlled by his business empire, Delaware Life Insurance Co. and Clear Spring Life and Annuity Co.

According to reports, federal prosecutors in Manhattan have been examining potential financial improprieties involving Walter’s companies. The investigation is focused in part on whether certain private credit investments were properly disclosed as related-party transactions. The FBI has also been involved in the broader probe.

Federal agents reportedly executed a search warrant in September 2025 and seized Walter’s mobile phone and computer while he was traveling through a Chicago airport. It remains unclear which specific part of the investigation prompted that seizure.

The scrutiny intensified in February 2026 when Delaware Life and Clear Spring received federal grand jury subpoenas. Regulatory filings later revealed that the insurers had significantly more exposure to related-party investments than previously reported. Delaware Life, for example, restated billions of dollars in investments after determining that certain transactions had been incorrectly classified. Reports have placed the revised exposure at more than $17 billion, while the Los Angeles Times described the change as roughly $1 billion to $16 billion.

Importantly, the investigation has not resulted in criminal charges against Walter or his companies. TWG Global has denied wrongdoing and said it is cooperating with authorities. The company has also stated that there was no fraud and no victim involved.

Against that backdrop, Racer’s report now links the federal scrutiny to the decision by GM to step away from conducting new business with Andretti’s IndyCar operation. That being said, it is confirmed that Honda’s engine supply relationship with Andretti will continue. For now, the reported GM decision appears to have closed the door on new business rather than disrupting Andretti’s current IndyCar operation.

Andretti’s long history with IndyCar engine partners

Andretti’s connection with Honda stretches back far beyond its two-year stint with Chevrolet. The partnership produced three IndyCar championships in 2004, 2005 and 2007, along with five Indianapolis 500 victories through 2017.

That history made Andretti’s return to Honda power in 2014 particularly significant. After competing with Chevrolet in 2012 and 2013, Michael Andretti described the reunion as being “back home.” Honda also welcomed Andretti back as an organization that had played a major role in its previous IndyCar success.

The timing also mattered. IndyCar was preparing for a new 2.2-liter, twin-turbocharged V6 engine formula for 2014. Both Honda and Chevrolet would use the mandated twin-turbo configuration, creating a fresh technical battle between the manufacturers.

Andretti was not simply returning to an old engine supplier. The organization was rejoining a manufacturer with which it had already developed considerable competitive familiarity.

The results after the reunion reinforced that connection. Andretti went on to win the Indianapolis 500 with Ryan Hunter-Reay in 2014, Alexander Rossi in 2016 and Takuma Sato in 2017, adding to its earlier Honda-powered victories with Dan Wheldon and Dario Franchitti.

That history helps explain why Honda remains important to Andretti’s IndyCar operation today. Racer’s report that Honda will continue supplying engines means the team retains a relationship that has delivered championships, Indy 500 victories and decades of shared racing experience.

For Andretti, the reported Chevrolet setback therefore does not force a major technical reset. Its Honda partnership remains in place, preserving a familiar foundation while uncertainty surrounds any future relationship with GM.

This article first appeared on EssentiallySports and was syndicated with permission.

title: After double dose of victory in Milwaukee, Pato O'Ward's name among legends
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
The list of IndyCar drivers who have won twice on the same day reads like a list of the greatest race drivers of all time: Mario Andretti, Al Unser, Bobby Unser, Dan Gurney, Johnny Rutherford and Rick Mears.

You can now add Pato O'Ward's name to that list after his sweep of the Milwaukee Mile on Sunday.

"Those are heavy names," O'Ward said. "Then you hear mine, you're like, what?"

O'Ward scored career wins 11 and 12 at the West Allis, Wis., track on Sunday and is only four points out of second in the championship going into the Sept. 6 season finale at Laguna Seca.

What Pato O'Ward said after Milwaukee sweep

"Honestly, man, I'm just writing my own story," he said. "I really don't know what's in store for my IndyCar career. So far I've dedicated my whole life to this. I always really dedicate myself to everything that I do to the best of my ability.

"I'm a hungry competitor. I love to go out there and compete and to challenge. It really is a bad day whenever we're not able to do that. I feel like this year there's been more of those than not."

O'Ward now has three victories this year, which account for all three of his podiums. While far from a perfect season, 2026 has been another solid campaign for the Monterrey, Mexico, native, who is building momentum towards 2027, where he hopes to take the fight to Alex Palou in the title race.

"If I keep doing that every race, for sure he's got no chance," O'Ward joked regarding Palou, who locked up a fourth straight championship and the fifth of his career at Milwaukee on Sunday. "I'll tell him, 'enjoy looking at my rear wing.' But right now I've been looking at his.

"The guy lives rent-free in everyone's head in the paddock. He's raised that bar, him and Ganassi. That 10 car has been unbelievable. Must be nice. One day we'll get there. One day we'll be there. It will be soon."

Quotes provided by IndyCar Media.

title: 'We're just cursed': David Malukas dealt another heartbreaking loss at Milwaukee
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Someday, Lady Luck will have to pay the piper and give David Malukas his first IndyCar victory.

Sunday was not that day.

Malukas led the first race of IndyCar's doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile on Sunday evening with 24 laps to go and was in prime position to pull away and finally score the first win of his career.

But an engine glitch on the race's final restart allowed Pato O'Ward to take the lead and drive to victory instead, leaving Malukas to finish runner-up.

— NTT INDYCAR SERIES (@IndyCar) August 30, 2026

It's another heartbreaking loss for Malukas, who was also on the losing end of the closest finish in the 110-year history of the Indianapolis 500 on May 24.

David Malukas thinks he's cursed

"I'm just so frustrated," Malukas told Fox Sports. "We had the car. We did everything right. We're just cursed. I literally believe I have some sort of curse. Everything was in our favor there. This weekend in both races we were having issues with the engine on restarts, coming out of the pits, needing to lift and having these events where we just lose power. That really let us down."

— INDYCAR on FOX (@IndyCarOnFOX) August 31, 2026

Malukas led 93 laps, second only to O'Ward, who led 119 in the victorious effort that gave him a sweep of the day's races at Milwaukee. By and large, Malukas has proved Roger Penske right in his decision to hire Malukas to drive the famed No. 12 Chevrolet.

Malukas is fifth in the standings through 17 races and was second for much of the year. He has an opportunity to finish runner-up in the championship depending on how things play out in the season finale at Laguna Seca on Sept. 6.

But coffee is, after all, for closers only, and so far, Malukas has been unable to close out a win either due to his own mistakes or horrendous strokes of luck.

Samuel Stubbs

Hailing from the same neck of the woods as NASCAR Hall of Famer Mark Martin, Samuel has been covering NASCAR for Yardbarker since February 2024. He has been a member of the National Motorsports Press Association (NMPA) since October of 2024. When he’s not writing about racing, Samuel covers Arkansas Razorback basketball for Yardbarker

title: Alex Palou is on pace to shatter IndyCar records like no driver has ever done
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Alex Palou is already one of the greatest IndyCar drivers of all time. In another decade, he might be looked at as the greatest the sport has ever seen.

That's because Palou, 29, already has 25 wins in only 115 starts and five championships in seven seasons. He locked up title No. 5, his fourth consecutive, Sunday at the Milwaukee Mile after a 10th-place finish in the first race of a doubleheader at the West Allis, Wis., track.

Though there's one more race at Laguna Seca on Sept. 6 left on the 2026 schedule — one that Palou will undoubtedly be the favorite to win, given that he won at the California road course last year — many eyes have already flipped to 2027 and the question of whether or not Palou can take home a sixth title and record fifth straight.

Records are often mentioned in conjunction with Palou's name due to the breakneck speed at which he breaks them. Previously, Palou's Chip Ganassi Racing teammate Scott Dixon was the fastest driver to five championships, winning those five titles over 15 seasons. Palou has done so in less than half the time and is on pace to win 10 championships in 14 years. He's easily the youngest five-time champ in series history.

Of course, it's not guaranteed that the Barcelona, Spain, native will race for another decade. But given that he's winning as frequently as he is, it's hard to imagine why he would want to stop.

All timer. We are witnessing history, written by one of the best to ever do it. https://t.co/puiZmfeuCq

— Will Buxton (@wbuxtonofficial) August 30, 2026

Alex Palou's thoughts on fifth title

"It's been incredible. I just feel like we just started yesterday," Palou said Sunday evening. "It just feels like we started yesterday. We're just getting closer and closer. We're having more fun and more fun each day. It's been an absolute joy of a year. The last two years have been just magical for us."

"I never thought I would be first of all an IndyCar driver. Never thought I could make it. Never thought that I would have the chance to be a professional race car driver. That was my dream. When I had the opportunity to be an IndyCar driver, that was already a huge achievement for me. I was living the dream. I remember also then Chip giving me that chance to drive for a championship-winning team at that moment. They just won in 2020 with Scott. That was mind-blowing. Since then I feel like I've been on this incredible cloud where everything has been so good for me... It's just super fun."

Palou is the first driver to win four straight titles since Sebastien Bourdais from 2004-07. Only Dixon, a six-time champion, and record-holder AJ Foyt, who won seven titles, are currently above him in the IndyCar zeitgeist.

It's very possible that, even with a new car coming to the IndyCar circuit in 2028 that will level the playing field, Palou could be tied with Foyt at seven championships at the end of his ninth season at age 31. By the end of 2029, it's a real possibility that no one will have ever won more IndyCar titles than Palou.

In regard to wins, the Spaniard has plenty of rungs to climb. He's "only" 17th all-time on the IndyCar win list at the moment, tied with Gordon Johncock and 42 victories behind Foyt, who holds the record with 67. Given that Palou won six races this year, it's not out of the question that he gets close to or surpasses Foyt in that category, either.

Ganassi isn't likely to let Palou walk in the next decade. Barry Wanser, Palou's strategist and the mastermind of the No. 10 team's continued success, isn't going anywhere anytime soon, either.

So long as the No. 10 CGR band stays together, Palou will continue to break records and write a legend that will be passed down for generations.

Quotes provided by IndyCar Media.

title: Alex Palou clinches 5th IndyCar title; Pato O'Ward sweeps Milwaukee twin bill
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Pato O'Ward had a day for the record book -- something Alex Palou knows all about.

While O'Ward won two IndyCar races in one day at the Milwaukee Mile, Palou did enough to clinch a historic IndyCar Series championship with one week to go Sunday in West Allis, Wis.

Weather delays forced the back-to-back race weekend into several schedule changes. Saturday's race, the Snap-on Makers and Fixers 250, was interrupted by heavy rain and moved to a Sunday evening finish after the regularly scheduled race, the Snap-on Milwaukee Mile 250.

O'Ward claimed them both, making the native of Mexico the first driver since Rick Mears in 1981 to win two IndyCar Series races in one day. Mears captured both halves of a doubleheader at Atlanta Motor Speedway that year.

Palou took fifth place in the Milwaukee Mile 250 and landed 10th in the nightcap, securing enough points for his fourth consecutive series championship and his fifth in six years.

The 29-year-old Spaniard is the youngest driver in IndyCar history to win five season titles. New Zealand's Scott Dixon holds the record with six, while A.J. Foyt won seven championships in the open-wheel racing series that preceded IndyCar. Palou broke a tie with Dario Franchitti of Great Britain.

"I don't know what to say," Palou told Fox Sports in his post-race interview. "I owe everything to this team, man. Everybody at Chip Ganassi Racing, Honda, DHL, all our partners, but especially Chip ... Incredible, man. Just so proud of this team."

Palou went on to say with a grin that it was hardly a good day for him on the track.

"Today was a really bad race for us," he said. "We were suffering all the time, but I was like, ‘Just keep focused, keep on going.'"

Palou has won six races this season and finished second in one other. With only the season finale to come next week in Monterey, Calif., Palou has a 100-point lead over second-place driver Christian Lundgaard of Denmark.

As for O'Ward, after he won the Milwaukee Mile 250 by 0.7916 seconds over Scott McLaughlin, he held the lead for the resumption of the Makers and Fixers 250. O'Ward finished the job, leading 119 laps and besting David Malukas by 1.7535 seconds.

Rinus VeeKay of the Netherlands, McLaughlin and Christian Rasmussen of Denmark finished third, fourth and fifth, respectively.

In one afternoon, O'Ward tripled his win total for the season, capturing his second and third titles of 2026.

"I've dreamt of weekends like this before," O'Ward said, "having the doubleheaders just a couple times in my career and wishing, like, ‘I want to win both of them in a week.' And we got to win both in a day. That's definitely a dream come true for myself and I'm sure for the team."

title: Pato O'Ward wins Milwaukee Mile 250 with postponed race still on tap
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Pato O'Ward claimed his second victory of the season Sunday by edging Scott McLaughlin at the Snap-on Milwaukee Mile 250 in West Allis, Wis.

The native of Mexico is in a rare position to win two races in one day after Saturday's Snap-on Makers and Fixers 250 was interrupted by heavy rain and postponed to a Sunday finish. O'Ward was in the lead when the race was suspended, and it will conclude Sunday evening at 5 p.m. local time.

"We were feeling really good yesterday, man," O'Ward said post-race. "I believe it's an all-Team Chevy podium. That's amazing. We like Milwaukee. Yesterday, car, like I said, was feeling really good.

"It took me a little bit to kind of find a rhythm. The track was a little bit hotter today, and it definitely makes these things a little bit more on the edge. But I used it up when we needed."

O'Ward took the lead for good on Lap 196 when Santino Ferrucci pitted and held it for the final 55 laps. He beat New Zealand's McLaughlin to the checkers by 0.7916 seconds, and his Arrow McLaren teammate Christian Lundgaard of Denmark was third.

David Malukas finished fourth, and Spanish star Alex Palou rounded out the top five. There's a chance Palou could clinch his fourth straight IndyCar Series championship and his fifth in six years before the end of the night.

Palou is 97 points ahead of second-place Kyle Kirkwood with only two races remaining: the delayed Milwaukee race and the season finale in Monterey, Calif., next Sunday. Per IndyCar, he only needs to hold a 54-point lead after the other race is completed to be assured of the title.

"We were going for the win today and didn't really have enough pace," Palou said after the regularly scheduled race. "Good opportunity tonight to get that championship. We know it's going to be tough, but we're going to try and fix the car a little bit and try to see if we can make it faster."

title: Pato O'Ward wins Snap-On Milwaukee Mile 250; Alex Palou inches closer to fifth IndyCar title
source: Yardbarker: IndyCar
excerpt:
Pato O'Ward won Sunday's NTT IndyCar Series race at the Milwaukee Mile while leading another race at the same time.

O'Ward was in the lead Saturday at the Milwaukee Mile when the remainder of the first race of the weekend's IndyCar doubleheader was pushed to Sunday due to rain. That race will resume around 6 p.m. ET, weather permitting, with coverage on FS1 and the IndyCar Radio Network.

O'Ward then went out and won Sunday's Snap-On Milwaukee Mile 250, beating Team Penske's Scott McLaughlin to the checkered flag by 0.7916 seconds.

"It took me a little bit to kind of find a rhythm," O'Ward told Fox Sports. "We had to car to do it, had the power to do it. Super proud of everybody."

O'Ward rebounded from a slow pit stop early in the race, and despite lapped traffic providing him a in the closing laps, he hung on to claim his second win of 2026 and the 11th of his IndyCar career.

Notable results

McLaughlin and Christian Lundgaard joined O'Ward on the podium, with David Malukas and Alex Palou rounding out the top five. Kyle Kirkwood, Rinus VeeKay, Christian Rasmussen, Marcus Ericsson and Louis Foster completed the top 10.

Other notable finishers include Santino Ferrucci in 12th, Mick Schumacher in 13th, Scott Dixon in 15th, Indianapolis 500 champion Felix Rosenqvist in 20th and Caio Collet in 23rd.

Romain Grosjean (24th) and Josef Newgarden (last, 25th) rounded out the field after crashes.

Palou had a chance to clinch the championship over Kirkwood in the first race of the day but was unable to do so. He holds a 97-point over Kirkwood ahead of the resumption of Saturday's race. The IndyCar season finale will take place at Laguna Seca on Sept. 6.

"That would be good," Palou said about clinching the championship. "We're going to try and fix the car a little bit, see if we can be better in a couple hours."

Palou is looking to claim his fifth championship and a fourth consecutive title on Sunday evening.
